entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bartholomew Columbus was a Genoese explorer and the younger brother of Christopher Columbus. Born in 1450 in Genoa, Italy, Bartholomew Columbus was educated in the art of navigation and shipbuilding, skills that would later serve him well in his own maritime endeavors. 



 As the younger brother of Christopher, Bartholomew was often overshadowed by his more famous sibling, but he carved out his own niche as a skilled navigator and cartographer. His most notable achievement was his role in the discovery of the island of Hispaniola, which he charted in 1493. 



 Bartholomew's contributions to the Age of Exploration had a lasting impact on the geography of the New World. His detailed maps and navigational charts helped to facilitate further European exploration and settlement of the Americas, cementing his place in the annals of history. 



 Despite his significant achievements, Bartholomew Columbus remained largely in the shadow of his more famous brother, a fact that was only rectified in recent years by historians who have sought to give him the recognition he deserves.
